subject: FastLine: intermittent completion failures and p99 spike — urgent
messages:
From: Sam Trent <sam.trent@fastline.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-08T09:12:34-07:00
Subject: Elevated p99 and failed completions — urgent

Hannah,

We started seeing a sharp degradation on our production calls to Redwood around 2027-07-07 18:00 UTC. p99 shot from ~1.1s to ~9.2s and we're also observing a ~12% failed-completion rate (timeouts / aborted). Overall throughput on our service dropped about 35% as requests queue up. This started as intermittent but has become sustained across our EU and US traffic windows.

I attached a trace bundle and a p99 timeseries snapshot. We need an urgent triage — this is affecting checkout flows and we are seeing a measurable drop in conversions. If this is related to any rolling change on your side, please call it out.

Sam
Ops, FastLine

Attachments: fastline_trace_bundle_20270708.tar.gz, p99_timeseries_20270708.png

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Trent <sam.trent@fastline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-08T09:28:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p99 and failed completions — urgent

Sam, thank you — I see the traces. I'm escalating immediately to our infra and support leads (cc'd). We will triage now and aim to come back in 2 hours with an initial hypothesis and mitigation plan.

Planned immediate actions:
- Ben + Karthik: quick analysis of queue/gpu backlog and per-tenant concurrency caps for FastLine (impact window: now -> +2h)
- Marissa: coordinate MAP and customer comms; set 30m sync if helpful
- We'll consider temporary routing to a lower-latency model variant or raising your concurrency cap while we stabilize.

Sam — can you confirm the account-level token rate and whether you had any recent traffic pattern changes? Also confirm whether you can accept a short maintenance window to apply a config change.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Trent <sam.trent@fastline.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-08T10:05:02-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p99 and failed completions — urgent

Sam — thanks for flagging. We understand the severity and will run this as a customer escalation. Quick asks so we can prioritize:
- Which endpoints are most impacted (publish the route names if possible)
- Any recent client-side SDK versions or batching changes?
- Confirm acceptable maintenance window (we can do an immediate 10-15m change if ok)

Immediate short-term options we can push in parallel:
1) Canary routing to a smaller model variant for 5% of requests while we triage (low risk, immediate)
2) Temporary per-account concurrency cap increase (needs infra sign-off)
3) Activate aggressive prefix/KV cache warmup on your account to reduce cold-cache tail

I'll coordinate communications and propose a 30-min check-in at 11:00 PDT.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-08T11:40:21-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p99 and failed completions — urgent

Quick triage notes after scanning the trace bundle + hot snippets:
- We see long GPU queue residency spikes correlated with batches that have large prefix variability from FastLine's traffic pattern — suggests KV cache churn / cold prefix cache misses (response tails)
- There are a non-trivial number of requests hitting the per-tenant concurrency cap which causes backpressure and queueing at the dispatcher layer rather than graceful shedding (we need to check policy knobs)
- A subset of traces show transient model OOM retries (GPU-side memory evictions) which can amplify queueing when retries pile up

Recommended immediate mitigations (fast, reversible):
1) Raise FastLine's concurrency cap from 80 -> 120 for the next 90 minutes in the dedicated routing pool (requires infra approval)
2) Enable aggressive KV cache pre-warm for their recent prefixes (no downtime, low risk)
3) If we see OOM-related retries persist, fall back 5% of traffic to a quantized variant that reduces memory pressure

I'll attach a small hottrace snippet for infra to inspect. If Karthik can OK (1) and (2) now we can monitor impact in 15m.

-ben

Attachments: hottrace_snippet.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-08T13:15:47-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated p99 and failed completions — urgent

Ben — good catch. I can apply (1) and (2) immediately but want to flag the potential cost/knock-on: raising per-tenant concurrency may increase contention for our dedicated pool and could cause marginal impact to other tenants if the pool is near capacity. FastLine is on a dedicated pool but we need to verify headroom.

Plan:
- I'll check pool headroom (5m) and if clear, apply the cap bump + enable KV warmup.
- I'll also push a short telemetry capture (heap / GPU queue lengths / nvml stats) and share dashboards to the INC-2345 ticket.
- If we see any sign of downstream impact, we will immediately revert and instead run the 5% model fallback.

Approve applying the changes? If approved I'll proceed and post metrics in 15m.

-karthik

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Trent <sam.trent@fastline.com>, Leah Park <leah.park@fastline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-08T14:02:11-07:00
Subject: Executive update: FastLine incident and next steps

Sam / Leah — short executive update on what we are doing and when you'll see improvement:

Summary of impact: sustained p99 tail increases and ~12% failed completions causing throughput degradation.
Actions taken / in progress:
- Applied a temporary per-account concurrency cap bump and enabled aggressive KV pre-warm for FastLine (applied at 13:22 PDT)
- Captured GPU queue/heap telemetry and traces; posted to INC-2345 (link above)
- Set a 5% canary fallback to a memory-friendly model variant if we see continued GPU OOM retries

What to expect: we expect visible p99 improvement within 10-20 minutes after config changes; we'll keep the cap change for 90 minutes while we stabilize and then step down in stages. If you prefer, we can keep the cap higher under a defined SLA credit during the window.

Next steps:
- 14:30 PDT check-in (Zoom link above) to review telemetry and confirm final rollout plan
- Post-incident writeup + long-term fixes: add auto-scaling headroom in routing pools for heavy-tail tenants, improve KV cache eviction heuristics, and tighten OOM early-warning alerts.

We will keep you closely updated; Marissa will own customer comms.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
